title: Smooth base change for the exceptional inverse image
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{\ u\ }&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{\ v\ }&Y
\end{array}
$$

be a Cartesian square in which $f$ is
smooth of pure relative dimension
$d$; the
ambient exceptional right
adjoint datum of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] is not assumed,
the right adjoints $Rf^!$, $Rf'^!$ that occur being, on the coefficients
used here, the theorem [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. Let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. The canonical
comparison

$$
Lu^*Rf^!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf'^!Lv^*K
$$

is an isomorphism. The morphism $v$ is arbitrary; its base change
$f'$ is smooth of the same relative dimension.

proof.text: At the positive finite stage, put l=P.coefficients.l and n=P.level. The spectral absolute value of l is its p-adic norm, strictly below one. The DVR description therefore puts l in m_E=(varpi_E), so l^n belongs to (varpi_E)^n and vanishes in A_{E,n}, including its ULift. The coefficient-prime unit theorem from the purity setting makes l a unit in every local ring of every scheme over k. Its nth power is a unit in the local rings, hence in global sections. This supplies HasInvertibleExponent for the actual finite coefficient ring, without requiring the ramification index to divide n.

source.place: Etale-origin representative, ordinary canonical smooth base change, and comparison of the actual finite-level functors.

proof.text: Unpack intrinsic bounded constructibility from the finite-Tor hypothesis on K after the canonical intrinsic realization R. A finite cohomological support has lower and upper bounds; their minimum and maximum give an ordered vanishing interval, also for empty support. Apply finiteRing_constructibleDerived_origin to R(K). It yields a bounded constructible etale L and an isomorphism D(C R)(L) ~= D(R)(K), where C is comparison inverse image. The exact-functor composition isomorphism and full faithfulness of the derived realization equivalence give C(L) ~= K. The lower endpoint of the interval makes L bounded below. This is an existence proof used only in a proposition; no data-valued definition chooses a witness.

proof.text: The derived comparison unit at the bounded-below etale L is invertible by site comparison. Apply C to that unit and use the left triangle identity to deduce that the comparison counit at C(L) is invertible. Counit naturality along C(L) ~= K transports invertibility to the counit at K.

source.place: Etale-origin representative, ordinary canonical smooth base change, and comparison of the actual finite-level functors.

proof.text: The right derived comparison restriction sends bounded-below objects to bounded-below objects, by its compatibility with the D+ right derived functor. Exact etale inverse image along v preserves this lower bound. The comparison unit at v_e^* Rnu_* K is therefore invertible. By definition smoothExceptionalComparisonMate is this unit followed by the right-derived comparison image of the inverse comparison-pullback isomorphism and of v_p^* applied to the counit at K. Every factor is invertible by the preceding step and functoriality. Thus this specific comparison-site mate is invertible, without an ambient pro-etale adjunction or a separate compact-support transpose computation.

source.place: Etale-origin representative, ordinary canonical smooth base change, and comparison of the actual finite-level functors.

proof.text: Convert the chosen Cartesian square to IsPullback. Base change preserves quasi-compactness and smoothness of pure relative dimension d; use c and c.ofIsPullback for the two compactification instances. Local finite type over the field base makes Y locally Noetherian, hence quasi-separated by typeclass inference. Apply the source-library form of prop-asd-smooth-base-change, AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.isIso_rightDerivedUpperShriekBaseChangeMap_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension, with the invertible exponent from step 1. It makes the ordinary canonical exceptional base-change transformation invertible at every etale complex, in particular Rnu_* K. Unfold only smoothExceptionalProEtaleBaseChangeMap: its first factor is the comparison-pullback isomorphism; its second is comparison inverse image applied to the inverse exact/derived etale pullback identification, this ordinary canonical exceptional map, and f-prime exceptional inverse image of the exact/derived v-pullback identification followed by the comparison-site mate from step 4. Functors preserve isomorphisms and composites of isomorphisms are isomorphisms. This proves the original IsIso conclusion for the specified arrow and the same-relative-dimension conclusion. All steps allow arbitrary v, empty schemes, K=0 and d=0.
